headline: Argentina Country Risk Surges Past 1,000 Points Amid Global Market Volatility
summary: Argentina's country risk index rose by 240 basis points in a single week to cross 1,000 points. The spike followed sharp declines in sovereign bond prices triggered by international risk aversion.
why: Argentina's country risk index measures the yield spread of sovereign debt over US Treasuries, signaling default probability and borrowing costs.

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: A 240-basis-point surge in sovereign risk raises borrowing costs for domestic issuers.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A global risk-off selloff in emerging market debt depressed Argentine bond prices.
